sections.title: Basic Concept of Error Spotting
sections.content: In Error Spotting, you have to find the grammatical error in a specific part of a sentence. Generally, the sentence is divided into 3-4 parts. Check in 2-3 steps: (1) Check Subject-Verb Agreement, (2) Check Nouns and Articles, (3) Check Prepositions and Tenses.

sections.title: Basic Subject-Verb Agreement
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the Subject. Step 2: Check if the Subject is singular or plural. Step 3: Use the verb accordingly. Example: 'Each of the boys is present.' Here, 'Each' is singular, so 'is' is correct; 'are' would be wrong.

sections.title: Common Noun Errors (Singular/Plural)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify whether the Noun is countable or uncountable. Step 2: Do not pluralize uncountable nouns. Example: 'Furnitures' is wrong, the correct word is 'Furniture'. 'Informations' is wrong, the correct word is 'Information'.

sections.title: Articles (A, An, The)
sections.content: Step 1: If the Noun starts with a vowel sound, use 'an'; if it starts with a consonant sound, use 'a'. Step 2: Use 'the' before specific nouns. Example: 'He is an honest man.' ('h' is silent in honest, so use 'an').

sections.title: Basic Prepositions (in, on, at)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify Time or Place. Step 2: Use the correct preposition. Use 'In' for months/years (in March), 'On' for days/dates (on Monday), 'At' for exact time (at 5 PM).

sections.title: Basic Tense Errors
sections.content: Step 1: Look for a time indicator (yesterday, since, now). Step 2: Choose the tense accordingly. Example: 'He has been working since 2020.' Here, 'since' indicates a starting point, so Present Perfect Continuous is correct.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Using a plural verb with 'Each', 'Everyone', 'Someone'. 2. Pluralizing uncountable nouns. 3. Omitting an article. 4. Using the wrong preposition.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Error Spotting, first check Subject-Verb agreement, then Nouns and Articles, and finally Prepositions and Tenses. Checking in these 2-3 steps can help catch most errors.

tricks.title: Each/Everyone Rule
tricks.explanation: Each, Everyone, and Someone are always considered singular.
tricks.example: Each of the students is ready. ('are' would be wrong)

tricks.title: Remember Uncountable Nouns
tricks.explanation: Information, Furniture, Advice, and Luggage do not have plural forms.
tricks.example: He gave me useful advice. ('advices' is wrong)

tricks.title: Vowel Sound Rule
tricks.explanation: Look at the sound, not the letter. If it is a vowel sound, use 'an'.

tricks.title: Time Preposition Shortcut
tricks.explanation: In = month/year, On = day/date, At = exact time.

tricks.title: Identifying Since/For
tricks.example: He has lived here since 2019. He has lived here for 5 years.

tricks.title: Plural Subject Check
tricks.explanation: Do not use a singular verb with a plural subject.
tricks.example: The players are ready. ('is' is wrong)

tricks.title: Correct Use of The
tricks.explanation: Use 'the' before unique or specific things.
tricks.example: The sun rises in the east.

tricks.title: Past Time = Past Tense
tricks.explanation: If you see words like yesterday or last year, use the Past tense.
tricks.example: He went home yesterday. ('goes' is wrong)

tricks.title: Distinguish Subject from Prepositions
tricks.explanation: Do not mistake a prepositional phrase for the main subject.
tricks.example: The list of items is long. (Subject = list)

tricks.title: Omission Check
tricks.explanation: Check if an article or preposition has been left out.
tricks.example: He is in the room. ('in room' is wrong)
